summary: Catalog cannot verify WHICH organizer a back-office request is for (TKT-236 ai-review)
description:
**Surfaced by TKT-236's ai-review.** Not a defect that ticket introduced — a property of the
deputy model that TKT-236 was the first to have to state out loud.

Catalog authenticates the **calling process**, not the staff member behind it. Every back-office
write takes `organizer_id` from the request body and catalog trusts it, because it has nothing else
to go on. The back office passes its session's organizer and never one from a form — but that is a
discipline in one codebase, not a boundary catalog can enforce.

TKT-236 narrowed the blast radius where it could: `UpdateChannel` now carries an organizer predicate,
so an id disclosed by the operator list is no longer sufficient to mutate another tenant's channel.
What remains is that a compromised or buggy back office can still *author for*, and now *enumerate*,
any organizer.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A way for catalog to verify which organizer a request is for, that does not rest on the caller
  asserting it. Options to weigh: a per-organizer credential; a signed assertion the back office
  mints from its session (commerce's customer-assertion key is the in-repo precedent); or catalog
  resolving the organizer from the staff identity it already stores.
- An ADR recording the choice and what it does *not* close — ADR-021's rule about naming the
  adversary applies: this is about a compromised deputy, not a DB writer.
- Applies to every catalog write the back office makes, not only channels. A fix that scoped one
  endpoint would leave the model unchanged and the claim still unearned.

Quality gates: `make check` green; `make browser` for any touched write form.

Non-goals: multi-organizer staff sign-in (ADR-042 scopes that as future work); inventory's credential
(TKT-244).

context.supersedes: 2026-08-10 bake (stale: ADR-056 and ADR-057 landed after it)

governingAdrs.why: Staff identity lives in catalog (staff_accounts, migration 0015); the BACK OFFICE owns the session and it is in-process and non-persisted. Sub-decision 4 scopes multi-organizer sign-in as out of scope, and sub-decision 2 promises the session module can be replaced 'without moving the enforcement point' -- which is the hinge for mechanism 3.

Where a service's auth guard lives: contract operation (declared security:, enforced by openapi3filter) vs internal route (inline header check). A new organizer-scoped credential or assertion must place itself on this line; catalog's writes are contract operations, so the guard belongs in the AuthenticationFunc seam.

Records the enumeration capability this ticket closes, and states the assumption explicitly: 'the back office is not compromised.' Its own code comment names TKT-245 as the owner of the fix (internal/api/server.go:323-325). Its reasoning deliberately does NOT generalize -- read the WHY IT DOES NOT GENERALIZE block before citing it as precedent.

NEW since the stale bake. The live in-repo template: a credential resolved to a scope {ResellerID, OrganizerID, ChannelCode} inside the AuthenticationFunc, handed to handlers through a per-request slot, with 'nothing in it ever comes from the request body'. It explicitly cites ADR-053's cross-tenant staff credential as the failure it avoids.

NEW since the stale bake. The freshest precedent for adding a service-specific staff credential (TKT-244), and it answers the same-shaped question as ADR-053 while reaching the OPPOSITE conclusion -- the difference is the whole content of that ADR. Read both before arguing from either.

Customer identity and storefront sessions -- the ADR behind commerce's customer assertion, which is mechanism 2's precedent. Its TKT-221 amendment records why a customer_id in the body and a service credential in the SSR process were BOTH refused; catalog's problem is the same shape with organizer_id.

Name the adversary. This ticket is about a compromised or buggy DEPUTY PROCESS, not a writer with catalog DB access -- no mechanism here constrains the latter, and the ADR must not overclaim. Three of its clauses broke this rule across two review passes.
Catalog owns organizers/tenants, which is why staff live there rather than in a sixth service or on the gateway.

governingTests.why: Derives the invariant from the SPEC in both directions over every operation: unsafe -> requires CatalogStaffWriteCredential AND declares 401; safe -> opts out with `security: []`. Adding a security scheme or a new operation without satisfying both fails the gate. This is why ADR-053 says catalog's contract cannot express a staff-authenticated GET.
Pins the scheme name and header to what the document declares. A header renamed in the spec but not in code would silently read a header nobody sends.
Refusals must not become an oracle. Any new refusal path (wrong organizer, bad assertion) has to answer identically to the existing ones.
The storefront must keep working. A change that makes reads demand an organizer identity breaks the public surface.

reference.summary: The corrected blast-radius reasoning and the residual it names -- it names TKT-245 as the owner of the fix. Read before anything else in the code.
Mechanism 2's precedent, in full: mint/verify an HMAC assertion `v1.<id>.<expiry>.<mac>`
Mechanism 1's precedent: credential -> scope in the AuthenticationFunc, per-request slot, never from the body
staff_accounts.organizer_id NOT NULL -- catalog already stores the fact it does not use
Catalog already returns the organizer at sign-in (StaffPrincipal.OrganizerId)
The back office reads staff.organizerId from its session and passes it as an argument
The existing guard seam a fix would extend
Browser-spec pattern for a back-office write form (make browser)
TKT-236 PR and its review (the finding this ticket was filed from)

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Filed from TKT-236 ai-review — incidental, deferred

**Finding:** [high] *"Credential widening materially increases compromise impact despite claiming
none."* The reviewer was **right about the claim**: the code said the added blast radius was nil, and
that was false — a create could only probe one guessed code at a time and never yielded an id, while
the list read returns every channel, id and disabled row in one call.

**Fixed in TKT-236:** the claim itself (corrected in the code and in ADR-053), and the chain it
enabled — `UpdateChannel` now carries an organizer predicate, so a disclosed id no longer mutates
across tenants.

**Deferred here:** the underlying model. Catalog cannot verify which organizer any back-office
request is for, on any endpoint. Closing that is a new credential or assertion mechanism affecting
every catalog write — its own vertical slice, not a channels story's.

Needs shaping before Gate 1: the choice between a per-organizer credential, a signed session
assertion, and catalog resolving the organizer from staff identity is the ticket's real content.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Shaping verdict — 6 of 8 met, 2 held for the human (Gate 1 blocked, correctly)

**Backend:** local tracker. **Gates:** all four waived for this ticket (owner, confirmed at start of
run); agent takes them by judgement, `overrides:` required at closeout.

#### The described defect survives verification — with one correction

TKT-250's lesson was that a filed ticket can describe a defect the code does not have, so this was
checked against HEAD before anything was planned. **It holds**, and the code says so in its own
words: `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:318-325` states the whole security property rests on
*"the back office is not compromised"* and names TKT-245 as the owner of the fix.

**The correction:** the ticket describes the problem as `organizer_id` **taken from the request
body**. That is 15 of catalog's 29 contract writes. The other 13 unsafe operations are
state transitions that take only a **path id** — `POST /series/{id}/publish`,
`/festivals/{id}/archive`, `/performances/{id}/close` and so on — and they reach the store with **no
organizer at any layer**: `PublishSeries(ctx, id uuid.UUID)` (`internal/store/store.go:696`,
`postgres.go:1055`). There is no asserted field to distrust because there is no field at all. A fix
shaped only around "don't trust the body value" would leave 13 writes untouched and the COS's
*"applies to every catalog write"* unearned — the exact failure the COS warns about, one level
deeper than it states.

#### What the read changed about the three mechanisms

The ticket presents three options as open. Reading the code narrows them:

**Catalog already knows the answer it fails to remember.** `staff_accounts.organizer_id` is
`NOT NULL REFERENCES organizers(id)` (migration `0015:21`) and `AuthenticateStaff` already returns it
as `StaffPrincipal.OrganizerId` (`internal/api/staff.go:76-80`). The back office learns the organizer
*from catalog* at sign-in, holds it in its session, and hands it back on every write — and catalog,
having said it, no longer knows it. The gap is not missing data; it is a missing binding between the
authenticated staff member and the request.

| # | Mechanism | Verified precedent | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Per-organizer credential | ADR-056 `partnerScope` — credential → `{ResellerID, OrganizerID, ChannelCode}` resolved in the `AuthenticationFunc`, *"nothing in it ever comes from the request body"* (`commerce/internal/api/partner_auth.go:36-43,103-115`) | Right shape, wrong caller. That credential authenticates a **machine** confined to one tenant. Catalog's is one env scalar (`CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`, `cmd/catalog/main.go:104`) shared by one back office serving *all* staff; per-tenant provisioning and rotation buys a boundary the signed-in human already carries. |
| 2 | Signed assertion minted from the session | commerce's customer assertion, `v1.<id>.<expiry>.<mac>`, HMAC-SHA256, minted on password presentation, kept server-side, forwarded on the write (`commerce/internal/api/assertion.go:57-72`); key already provisioned by `scripts/env-bootstrap.sh:72` | **Recommended.** Commerce hit the *identically shaped* problem in TKT-221 — session in one process, identity needed in another, `customer_id` in the body forgeable — and this is the answer it landed on, reviewed and shipped. Catalog's is the same with `organizer_id`. It also fits the existing seam: `authenticateStaffWrite` is already the `openapi3filter` `AuthenticationFunc` (`write_credential.go:29`), which is where ADR-056 proves a scope can be attached. |
| 3 | Catalog resolves the organizer from staff identity | ADR-042 sub-decision 2: the session module can be replaced *"without moving the enforcement point"* | Cleanest **end state** and where ADR-042 points, but it means catalog owns sessions — a table, a migration, an expiry sweep, and moving enforcement out of the back office. Larger than this ticket; mechanism 2 is a strict step toward it, not a detour, since the mint/verify seam is the same one a session would later use. |

⚠️ **ADR-053 must not be cited as precedent without reading its `WHY IT DOES NOT GENERALIZE` block**,
and ADR-057 answers a same-shaped question while reaching the **opposite** conclusion. Both are in
the refreshed mémo with that warning attached.

#### Scope is too large for one ticket — proposed slice

28 writes (excluding `authenticateStaff` itself) across **two classes that do not share a remedy**.
SPIDR, split on Rules/Interface:

- **Slice 1** — the mechanism, the verification seam, and the **15 body-organizer writes**. Per
  AGENTS.md the target is **unsubmittable, not validated**: delete `organizer_id` from the request
  types rather than comparing it, or the trust boundary stays in the client and only moves.
- **Slice 2** — the **13 path-id transitions**. A store-tier scoping change (organizer predicate on
  lookup), not a credential change. Different tier, different tests, different failure mode.

Recommending the split be confirmed **at Gate 1** rather than discovered mid-Planning.

#### Readiness

| Item | State | One-liner |
|---|---|---|
| `objective` | **met** | Verified at HEAD; the code names this ticket as its fix. |
| `scope` | **met** | In/out drawn; multi-organizer sign-in and inventory explicitly out. |
| `uncertainties` | **met** | Resolved by reading; surfaced the unstated 13-transition class. |
| `dependencies` | **met** | No open blockers; precedents already shipped. |
| `approach` | **open**, `owner: human` | Trust-boundary decision on an auth surface — `deferred` is barred by `shaping.md`. |
| `first_slice` | **open**, `owner: human` | Follows from `approach`; the 15/13 split needs confirming. |
| `success` | **met** | COS sharpened: unsubmittable, adversary named, omission enumerated both ways. |
| `context_memo` | **met** | Re-resolved 2026-08-15; +ADR-056, +ADR-057, +4 governing tests; all 8 ADRs verified present at HEAD. |

**Gate 1 is hard-blocked while `approach` and `first_slice` are open — as intended.** Both are
questions only the owner can answer, and both are in the agent's message alongside this comment.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 decisions recorded + shaping addendum (2 findings from a second read)

#### The owner's answers (both `open` items now `met` — Gate 1 unblocked)

**`approach` → mechanism 2, the signed assertion.** Catalog mints an HMAC organizer assertion at
`POST /staff/authenticate`, the back office holds it server-side in its existing session and forwards
it as a header, catalog verifies it in the `openapi3filter` `AuthenticationFunc` seam and takes the
organizer from the verified payload. **`organizer_id` is deleted from the 15 request types** —
*unsubmittable, not validated*, per AGENTS.md and the three passes TKT-244 spent learning it.

**`first_slice` → slice 1 = mechanism + seam + the 15 body writes.** The 13 path-id transitions
become a follow-up ticket: a store-tier organizer predicate, not a credential change, sharing no code
with this slice.

#### Addendum — two sites a second read found, both belonging to slice 1

A follow-up pass over the whole surface (not just the contract) turned up two places the
15-body-writes framing does not cover, and both would leave the claim half-true if missed:

**1. `GET /internal/channels` takes a caller-supplied `organizer_id` in the QUERY STRING**, under the
same staff-write credential (`internal/api/channels.go:115`, guarded by `staffMayReadOperatorChannels`
at `server.go:344`). This is the *exact* enumeration capability ADR-053 recorded and that this ticket
was filed to close — and it is not a body field, so a fix shaped only around request bodies sails
past it. It is one route, it is in the same guard seam, and leaving it would mean shipping "catalog
verifies the organizer" while the enumeration path that motivated the ticket still trusts the caller.
**Recommend it joins slice 1.**

**2. `DEFAULT_ORGANIZER_ID` is still a live fallback in the back office.**
`web/backoffice/src/lib/catalog.ts:69` hardcodes `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001` and it is a
**default parameter** on six functions — `getVenues` (:72), `getVenue` (:85), `createSeatMap` (:131),
`addSeatMapSection` (:143), `addSeatMapRow` (:154), `addSeatMapSeat` (:165), `updateVenueGaCapacity`
(:233). Every current call site passes `staff.organizerId` explicitly, so nothing is broken today, but
the fallback is reachable by any caller that omits the argument, and its own comment says *"When admin
auth lands this comes from the session."* This ticket **is** that landing. These signatures have to
change anyway once catalog stops accepting a body organizer, so deleting the default belongs here
rather than surviving as a silent tenant-defaulting path.

Contrast, already correct and worth preserving: the event and channel authoring functions take
`organizerId` as a **required first parameter with no default**, for the reason stated at
`catalog.ts:303-305` — *"a default here is how one organizer's staff would author into another's
tenant."*

#### One count correction

The contract yields **15** body-carried writes (all with `organizer_id` **required**), enumerated by
reading `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`: `createVenue`, `createSeatMap`, `addSeatMapSection`,
`addSeatMapRow`, `addSeatMapSeat`, `editSeatMap`, `updateVenueGaCapacity`, `createEvent`,
`createPerformance`, `createSeries`, `createSeason`, `createFestival`, `createTicketType`,
`createChannel`, `updateChannel`. Slice 1 is therefore **15 writes + 1 guarded read + the back-office
default** — not 14, and not 28.

#### Note for the planner on the pricing/fees surface

`CreatePriceRule`, `CreateFeeRule`, `CreatePayee` and `CreateSplitSchedule` exist in the store
(`internal/store/store.go:599-629`) with **no HTTP endpoint and no caller**. They are not in scope and
must not be "fixed" — but a drafter grepping for organizer-carrying writes will find them, so they are
named here as deliberately excluded rather than missed.

#### Readiness: 8 of 8 met — Gate 1 clear

`objective` · `scope` · `uncertainties` · `dependencies` · `approach` · `first_slice` · `success` ·
`context_memo` — all **met**. No open blockers. Ready to claim.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed → Planning

**Branch:** `TKT-245-organizer-assertion` off `origin/main` @ `be4bb5d7`.
**Blockers:** none (no `links` on the ticket; readiness 8/8 `met`).

**Why this one:** it is the ticket the code names as its own fix
(`services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:323-325`), and it was shaped and decided in this session —
mechanism and slice are settled, so Planning has no pending human call to stall on.

#### Risk verdict — **`risk:low` NOT claimed**

Stated explicitly rather than left to inference, because the label's carve-outs are exactly the
tickets whose risk is obvious to the claimer and invisible in the thread afterwards (TKT-190).

This ticket hits **three** of the four carve-outs:

- **auth** — it changes a trust boundary. This is the entire content of the ticket.
- **>5 files** — 15 request types, the mint site, the verify seam, the back-office session and client,
  the contract, plus tests and an ADR.
- **CI/deploy config** — a new signing key must be provisioned (`scripts/env-bootstrap.sh`,
  `scripts/stack-env.sh`, `compose.yaml`), following `COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY`'s precedent.

The plan gate would therefore be mandatory. It is **waived for this run by the owner** (all four
gates, agent's judgement, `overrides:` required at closeout) — waived, not inapplicable, and the
distinction is the point of writing it down.

#### Gate-2 posture under the waiver

The plan draft goes to `gpt-5.6-luna` via the codex runner (`config.models.plan`), critiqued by
`main-agent` (`config.models.planReview`) — the two differ, so the cross-model invariant holds and no
degraded flow is being run. I take Gate 2 on the strength of that critique.

**One thing I will be watching for**, flagged now so it is on the record before the draft exists: the
mechanism must not become *"validate the submitted organizer"*. If, after the change, the question
*"can the client influence which organizer catalog writes to?"* still answers **"yes, but only if it
lies in a way I now check for"**, it is not fixed (AGENTS.md; TKT-244 took three passes and a
capability deletion to learn it). The target is that `organizer_id` is **absent from the request
types**, not compared.

objective.note: Catalog authenticates the calling PROCESS, not the staff member behind it. Verified at HEAD: 15 of 29 contract writes take organizer_id from the request body and catalog trusts it (services/catalog/internal/api/server.go, channels.go); the back office passes staff.organizerId from its session (web/backoffice/src/pages/channels.astro:72,90,107,135) and never a form value -- a discipline in one codebase, not a boundary catalog enforces.

scope.note: IN: an organizer identity catalog verifies independently of the request body, applied across the whole back-office write surface; the ADR recording the choice and its residual. OUT: multi-organizer staff sign-in (ADR-042 sub-decision 4 scopes it as future work); inventory's credential (TKT-244/ADR-057); commerce and access surfaces. See first_slice -- the surface splits into two classes that do not have the same fix.

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading, not asking. (1) staff_accounts ALREADY carries organizer_id NOT NULL REFERENCES organizers(id) (migration 0015:21), and AuthenticateStaff already returns it as StaffPrincipal.OrganizerId (internal/api/staff.go:76-80) -- catalog already knows the fact it fails to remember. (2) The back-office session is in-process and its token is opaque (ADR-042 sub-decision 2; web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts:10-11), so catalog cannot verify a session cookie -- any fix must carry the organizer in something catalog can check itself. (3) A second, UNSTATED exposure class: 13 state-transition writes take only a path id and reach the store with no organizer at any layer (store.PublishSeries(ctx, id) -- internal/store/store.go:696, postgres.go:1055). Those have no field to compare, so the body-field framing in the ticket text does not cover them.

dependencies.note: No open blockers. Depends on decisions already landed, not on unshipped work: ADR-056's partnerScope is a working in-repo template for exactly this (credential -> scope resolved in the AuthenticationFunc, 'nothing in it ever comes from the request body' -- services/commerce/internal/api/partner_auth.go:36-43,103-115), and it names ADR-053's staff credential reaching across tenants as the anti-pattern it was written to avoid (:105-107).

approach.note: DECIDED by the owner at Gate 1 (2026-08-15): mechanism 2, an HMAC-signed organizer assertion. Catalog mints it at POST /staff/authenticate (it already holds the organizer there -- internal/api/staff.go:78); the back office keeps it server-side in its existing in-process session (web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts:53-56, the Entry interface gains a field exactly as the storefront's did) and forwards it as a header on writes; catalog verifies it in the openapi3filter AuthenticationFunc seam and takes the organizer from the verified payload. organizer_id is DELETED from the 15 request types -- unsubmittable, not validated (AGENTS.md). Modelled on commerce's customer assertion (services/commerce/internal/api/assertion.go), which solved the identically-shaped problem in TKT-221.

first_slice.note: DECIDED by the owner at Gate 1 (2026-08-15): slice 1 = the mint/verify mechanism, the verification seam, and the 15 body-organizer writes. The 13 path-id transitions become a follow-up ticket -- they need a store-tier organizer predicate, not a credential change, and share no code with this slice. See the kind=readiness addendum for the two extra sites that belong to slice 1 for consistency (GET /internal/channels' query-string organizer, and the back office's DEFAULT_ORGANIZER_ID fallback).

success.note: From the ticket, sharpened by the read: (1) catalog determines the organizer for a back-office write without the caller asserting it -- make it UNSUBMITTABLE rather than validated (AGENTS.md; TKT-244 took three passes to learn this); (2) an ADR naming the adversary per ADR-021 -- a compromised deputy PROCESS, not a DB writer -- and stating what stays open; (3) coverage across the sliced surface, with omission enumerated in both directions. Gates: make check green; make browser for any touched write form (test/browser/channels.mjs is the pattern).

context_memo.note: Re-resolved at claim time. The 2026-08-10 bake was stale: ADR-056 and ADR-057 both landed after it and both bear on the central decision. All 8 cited ADRs verified to resolve to real files at HEAD. governingTests added -- catalog's contract invariant is enforced by a TEST, not an ADR, and is discoverable only by failing the gate.
